figures.alt: Illustration of two teams of teenagers pulling on a rope in a tug of war. The red ribbon at the middle of the rope has not moved from the center.
figures.caption: Equal pulls in opposite directions are balanced. The rope does not change its motion.

figures.alt: Two pictures of a small red toy car on a wooden table. Left: a hand pushes the car, and a green arrow pointing right and a red arrow pointing left are about the same length, so the pushes are balanced and the car keeps the same speed. Right: the green arrow pointing right is much longer than the red arrow pointing left, and motion lines trail the car, so the pushes are unbalanced and the car speeds up.
figures.caption: Left, balanced: the pushes are equal, so the car keeps the same speed. Right, unbalanced: the push is bigger, so the car speeds up.

figures.alt: Interactive: sliders set the push from each side on a puck on ice, starting at rest or already sliding, and a run shows whether its speed changes.
figures.caption: Push a hockey puck from both sides on a smooth floor or ice and see what balanced and unbalanced forces do.

figures.alt: A long wooden ruler lying on a floor with four blue balls in a row along it, each the same distance from the next.
figures.caption: A ball that goes the same distance every second has a steady speed. A ball that goes less each second is slowing down, because friction pushes against it.

figures.alt: Interactive: a mark drops every second under a rolling ball. On ice the distances between marks stay equal, on a real floor they shrink.
figures.caption: Roll a ball on ice (like a frozen puddle) or on a real floor, and read how far it goes each second.

figures.alt: A sorting tray with two sections and a red horseshoe magnet above it. On the left, a paper clip and a steel nail are pulled up toward the magnet. On the right, a penny, a piece of aluminum foil, an eraser and a brown stone stay still.
figures.caption: Left side: sticks. Right side: does not stick. A magnet pulls on the paper clip and the nail. It does not pull on the penny, the foil, the eraser or the stone.

figures.alt: Side view of a cardboard sheet resting like a bridge on two stacks of books, with a paper clip on top, a magnet held under the cardboard, and a flag at the finish line.
figures.caption: Side view: a cardboard sheet rests like a bridge on two stacks of books. A paper clip sits on top. A magnet under the cardboard moves the clip toward a finish line 20 cm (about 8 inches) away. No one touches the clip.

figures.alt: Interactive: drag a horseshoe magnet around a table. A paper clip, a steel nail, a steel key and iron filings jump to the magnet as it gets close. A wooden block, a plastic cap, a penny, an eraser, aluminum foil, a Petoskey stone and a piece of copper never move.
figures.caption: Magnet sandbox. The pull gets weaker the farther away the magnet is, so it works without touching.
